subject: FastTrack launch: enablement handoff & exception routing
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: Mike Zhang <mike@acmecloud.com>
Date: Sun, 04 Oct 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: FastTrack launch: enablement handoff & exception routing

Team —

Quick status and asks for FastTrack (pilot) as we move toward the tentative production window (Oct 20–22): product signoff is on track pending a final run of the integration smoke tests next week. Before we lock the go/no-go I need a short, concrete enablement plan and exception routing so Sales / Customer Success have predictable fallbacks.

Key asks (owners in parentheses):
- Customer-facing enablement doc (what to show, runbook snippets, feature caveats). Owner: marissa_cole. Due: Oct 11.
- Training: 45m live demo + FAQ doc for CS and Sales. Owner: lauren_bishop. Due: Oct 13.
- Ops exception matrix: what to do when inference latency or token limits exceed thresholds, fallback model mapping and rollout rollback lane. Owner: vivek_kulkarni. Due: Oct 12.
- Pricing/credit escalation (Ben): quick decision path if they request temporary increased throughput while we validate.

I attached the release summary we circulated to Execs (fasttrack_release_summary.pdf) — use that for framing. Two specific questions I want answered in replies: 1) Are there any non-negotiable docs or runbook items that would block go? 2) Do we need an SLA carve-out for the pilot that Legal needs to sign?

I will consolidate replies and run a 30-min alignment on Oct 14 if we have the artifacts. If anything looks like it needs a fast exception (e.g., a customer cannot accept the normal latency SLO during pilot), flag it and add a short rationale in your reply.

Thanks — Soojin
Soojin Lee
Head of Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: fasttrack_release_summary.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com

Date: Sun, 04 Oct 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FastTrack launch: enablement handoff & exception routing

Thanks Soojin — assigning the doc work. Quick notes:

- I will own the customer-facing enablement doc. Plan is: one-pager features + 2 runbook snippets (staging repro steps, how to escalate to infra).
- I uploaded a working checklist (fasttrack_enablement_checklist.xlsx) with proposed sections and a skeleton schedule for the training sessions.
- Question for Product: do we need to surface the quantization/accuracy tradeoffs to the pilot customer in the doc or keep it internal? My inclination: small callout in the FAQ explaining expected variation vs. GA.

Link to the doc skeleton and template I will use: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/c/FASTTRACK-Enablement

If no objections, I'll circulate the first draft by Oct 9 and set the training slot placeholder for Oct 14 10:00am PT (45m). Lauren — if that conflicts with other training commitments, let me know and propose alternatives.

—Marissa
Principal Developer Relations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: fasttrack_enablement_checklist.xlsx
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: Mike Zhang <mike@acmecloud.com>, Eva Torres <eva@pilotpartners.io>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FastTrack launch: enablement handoff & exception routing

Looping in Sales perspective and an ask for a mutual action plan.

Quick points:
- Mike at Acme (pilot contact) asked whether we can temporarily route requests to a higher-capacity pool if they hit sustained bursts during the first 48 hours. That would require an SLA carve-out or a short-term credit arrangement. I need a recommendation from Finance/Revenue (I can coordinate) but product needs to sign off on fallback compatibility.
- For the exception plan: Vivek, can we document a clear cascade (primary model -> quantized variant -> fallback hosted model) and the exact trigger thresholds? Sales needs deterministic answers.

Inline reply to Marissa: please add an explicit "customer-facing fallback" section (one paragraph) describing expected behavior plus a link to the public-facing FAQ. Keep the technical runbook separate.

On quoting Soojin: "If anything looks like it needs a fast exception... flagging now: Acme may request temporary throughput increase. If we say yes, we should also note the operational cost and timeline for enabling extra capacity so Sales isn't surprised."

Ben
Head of Growth — Redwood Inference

Thanks — quick ops response and a proposal attached (prod_exception_matrix.pdf). TL;DR:

- Canary plan: 10% traffic slice over the first 12 hours with telemetry checks at 15m intervals.
- Cascade/fallback sequence we will document: primary model (v1.3 FP16) -> quantized variant (v1.3-int8) -> hosted fallback (redwood-hosted-small-latency). Triggers: 95th percentile latency > 1.5x target for 5m OR error rate > 1% for 3m.
- Temporary capacity increase: we can enable a provisional capacity bump but it requires a signed short-term amendment (Finance/legal). Ben, if Sales confirms they will cover the incremental unit costs during the 48h window we will route.
- Production exception matrix attached for review. If no objections, I'll publish the matrix to the FastTrack Confluence page and update the canary schedule in the shared calendar.

Action items assigned:
- Vivek: publish matrix + implement canary config (due Oct 8).
- Marissa: publish customer-facing fallback paragraph in the enablement doc (due Oct 9).
- Lauren: lock training slot and prepare demo script that highlights fallbacks (due Oct 13).
- Ben: confirm commercial/credit path with Finance and reply with recommended wording for the pilot amendment (due Oct 9).

I'll run the canary dashboard during the first window and post telemetry links in the shared thread.

Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Production Services
Redwood Inference

Attachment: prod_exception_matrix.pdf
